scopeNotes: The broad Seminole polygon covers Florida; the five named reservation records are separate places belonging to one modern tribal government. Each has a dedicated narrative section. The Oklahoma record is not included.

Every imported interval is 1492 to 1500, an anachronistic placement for modern reservations. Exact boundaries remain unverified; the Tampa geometry is a degenerate point-sized feature. No border edits or historical lifetime claims are made.
Reservation records are classified as regions to distinguish places from independent states. The broad Seminole record is a people or culture.
The narrative distinguishes the Florida tribal government, the broader Seminole history and the Miccosukee Tribe; it does not turn shared ancestry into one present-day government.

Named buildings and numbered archival photographs provide concrete historical examples. No museum acquisition is described as an excavation, and reservation archaeology is not automatically assigned a modern ethnicity.

The Tribe’s older chickee and clothing pages contain dated generalizations. Only specific construction, textile and historical evidence is used; superiority claims and claims that all families lived alike are omitted.
No present-day officeholders, enterprise rankings, population estimates or unsettled legal interpretations are asserted. Source publication dates are separate from the events described.
Independent review, chronological and geometry correction, and depth certification remain pending. No modern country is linked as a successor to a continuing people.
